rules: Benefit sentences use 'your [teams]' as the subject.
'We' appears only in mechanism, belief and founder copy, never in a benefit sentence.

headline_terminal_periods.rule: A headline takes a period ONLY when it is two or three parallel fragments. One clause = no terminal punctuation.

proof_block_ratio.rule: Roughly one content block in three is a proof block on any page that sells the product.

verbs.rule: ~20 concrete operational verbs, all base-form imperatives. No abstract verbs of enablement (empower, enable, unlock, transform, streamline) in the brand's own voice.

solution.note: every hit is the customer name 'Creative Solutions in Healthcare', an advisor title, or a customer quote - never the product

other: no exclamation marks in brand voice
no urgency language on product pages
no footnotes or sources on stats

rationed_superlatives.rule: each superlative is anchored to a checkable axis, e.g. 'more referral platforms, hospital systems, and EHRs than any platform on the market'

numbers.style: numerals only, compact unit, <=2 significant figures, no source, no footnote
conventions: '+' suffix means 'at least' and does persuasion work (2,000+, $380K+, 40%+)
'~' appears only inside customer quotes; the brand never hedges its own number
a raw duration beats a percentage when the duration is small (7 min, not 83% faster)
numbers are spelled out only in running prose ('less than five minutes'), never in a stat
stat template: [numeral][compact unit][+] / [2-9 word lowercase noun phrase]

growth: 40%+ of managed care days in L2+
time_returned: 34 hrs saved for care staff each week

product.rule: The product name is used as a grammatical SUBJECT that acts: '[product] reads / pulls / consolidates / centralizes ...'

rules: unit noun changes per segment: skilled nursing = 'buildings', home health/hospice = 'branches'

rule: exactly one italic per line, never two
never the first word of the line
never a product name, never a number, never a proper noun (one conventional exception: a publication title in a bio)
it always lands on the word the sentence turns on - remove it and the sentence keeps its grammar but loses its point
scarcity is the mechanism: 15 italics against 130 headings on the core pages (~1 in 9)
